    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	/--
    27	A finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question
    28	pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
    29	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
    30	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.
    31	-/
    32	structure Game where
    33	  QuestionA : Type
    34	  QuestionB : Type
    35	  AnswerA : Type
    36	  AnswerB : Type
    37	  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]
    38	  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]
    39	  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]
    40	  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]
    41	  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]
    42	  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
    43	  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]
    44	  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]
    45	  μ : Distribution (QuestionA × QuestionB)
    46	  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
    47	  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool
    48	
    49	attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
    50	  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
    51	  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq
    52	
    53	/--
    54	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
    55	is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
    57	is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
    58	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    59	-/
    60	noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    61	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    62	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    63	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
    64	  M.postprocess Prod.fst
    65	
    66	/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
    67	`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
    68	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    69	-/
    70	noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    72	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    73	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
    74	  M.postprocess Prod.snd
    75	
    76	/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
    78	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
    79	def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    80	    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
    81	  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)
    82	
    83	/--
    84	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
    87	-/
    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
    99	
   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   124	private noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/--
   132	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   133	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   134	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   136	-/
   137	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   138	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   139	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   140	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   141	
   142	/--
   143	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   144	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   145	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   146	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   147	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   148	intentionally not asserted here.
   149	-/
   150	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   151	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
   152	
   153	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

# Lean Proof Integrity Rules

This file is the **single source of truth** for proof integrity checks in this
repository. All CI workflows and review prompts should reference this file
rather than duplicating the rules inline.

> **Lean version**: 4.x (Lean 3 keywords like `constant` do not apply)

> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues
> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check below yet still
> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,
> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default
> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).
> Consult it alongside this file during review.

> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a
> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`
> blocker below may be temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The
> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof
> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the
> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a
> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or
> conditional helper
> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.
> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge
> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.

---

## Blockers

These patterns **must** be resolved before merging.

### Direct proof holes

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `sorry` | Axiomatically closes any goal — the proof is incomplete |
| `admit` | Tactic alias for `sorry` |

### Kernel / type system bypasses

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `native_decide` | Relies on trusted native evaluation / compiler; banned in Mathlib for soundness and process reasons |
| `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce` | Type system bypass — can fabricate any proof term |
| `lcProof` | Low-level proof fabrication primitive — can prove `False` |
| `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat` | Kernel reduction primitives exploitable for unsound proofs |

### Axiom smuggling

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `axiom` declarations | Introduces unproven assumptions that could be inconsistent; must be explicitly justified |

When an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,
prefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`
declaration, and add a regression check (for example a
`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in
`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen
the axiomatic base.

This preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper
theorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a
caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a
proof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly
conditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement
faithful to the paper.

### Circular reasoning

Lean's kernel forbids literal declaration cycles, so focus on **mathematical
circularity**:

- Proofs that assume (or trivially reintroduce) the statement being proved as a
  local hypothesis, then immediately close the goal from that hypothesis
- Helper lemmas in the same file that essentially restate the main goal and are
  only used to prove that goal
- Local `have`/`let` bindings that are just the goal rephrased, used to solve
  the goal without any real argument
- Newly introduced `axiom` that makes a difficult statement trivially provable
  without connecting to existing Mathlib / core theorems
- Abuse of `unsafe` features to fabricate proofs instead of giving a genuine
  derivation
- `by exact h` where `h` came from an unjustified assumption identical to the
  goal

### Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)

Proofs that avoid grounding in Mathlib:

- Custom re-declarations of standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., re-proving
  `add_comm` instead of importing it)
- `axiom` or `sorry`-based helper lemmas for facts that already exist in
  Mathlib
- Chains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core
- `private` helper lemmas that duplicate Mathlib API (e.g., custom matrix
  transpose lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)
- Overly long proof chains replaceable by a single Mathlib lemma

When flagging, perform an actual lookup (grep, `#find?`, `exact?`,
`library_search`). If an equivalent exists, cite the Mathlib lemma and module
path. If not, state "no equivalent found" with search evidence.

### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization

This is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or
theorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,
making them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.

Signs to watch for:

- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,
  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's
  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)
- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types
  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions
- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical
  semantics (e.g., a "projective measurement" definition that does not enforce
  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)
- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be
  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything
- Definitions that "work" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to
  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,
  incompatible universes)

When reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of
this?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the
scaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks
progress rather than enabling it.

### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift

A theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker
if its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.
Changing a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is
strongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a
documented mathematical necessity.

The most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an
extra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional
theorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not
repair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named
`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,
generic `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those
assumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.

Conditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet
be closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a
named lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional
helper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named
obligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show
that it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or
`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled
blueprint theorem with `\leanok`.

Existing bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs
for reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a
strengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the
bridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is
to restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a
tracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.

Not every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed
to encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model
instances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be
faithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These
conditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is
mathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate
step of the source proof.

For every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:

- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;
- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;
- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened
  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.

---

## Warnings

These should be flagged for review but may be acceptable with justification.

### Placeholder tactics

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`, `suggest` | Search tactics left as placeholders — replace with the concrete result |

### Safety / termination bypasses

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `unsafe def` | Bypasses Lean safety checks; should not appear in proof-relevant code |
| `partial def` | No termination proof required; unsound if used to build proof terms |
| `implemented_by` / `implementedBy` | Decouples runtime behavior from proven specification |

### Suspicious options

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `set_option maxHeartbeats 0` | Disables timeout — can hide non-terminating proofs |
| `set_option maxHeartbeats` with values >= 4,000,000 | 20x the default (200,000) — likely indicates an inefficient proof |
| `set_option maxRecDepth` with values >= 10,000 | May hide structural issues in proofs |

### Debug artifacts

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `dbg_trace` | Debug trace left in code |
| `stop` | Halts elaboration — development aid only |
| `#check`, `#eval`, `#print` in proof files | Debug commands that should be removed |

---

## How to use this file

**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read
[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a
proof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation
structure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why
conditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a
tracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.

**In CI review prompts**: Reference this file instead of inlining the rules:
```
Read `docs/PROOF_INTEGRITY.md` for the complete list of proof integrity
rules. Flag blockers as must-fix issues that should block merge.
Flag warnings as advisory — note them but acknowledge they may be
acceptable with justification.
```

**For manual review**: Use this as a checklist when reviewing Lean PRs.

**Updating rules**: Edit this file and all referencing workflows will
automatically pick up the changes.

   508	  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases k <;> fin_cases l <;>
   509	    simp [commute_iff_eq, msConstraintVars, msCellObservable,
   510	      heteroKron_mul, hOA, hOB, hac, qubitX_sq, qubitZ_sq,
   511	      qubitX_mul_qubitZ, hA_BA, hBA_A, hB_BA, hBA_B, hZ_ZX,
   512	      hZX_Z, hX_ZX, hZX_X, heteroKron_neg_left,
   513	      heteroKron_neg_right]
   514	
   515	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for
   516	`exists_ms_perfect_strategy_of_anticommuting` (`thm:ms-from-ac`, blueprint
   517	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:257-267`): the three observables of a Magic Square
   518	constraint multiply to `1` for the five even constraints and to `-1` for the
   519	last one, which is the anticommuting column of the operator table. -/
   520	theorem msConstraintObservable_product
   521	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
   522	    (OA OB : Op V) (hOA : OA * OA = 1) (hOB : OB * OB = 1)
   523	    (hac : OA * OB = -(OB * OA)) (i : Fin 6) :
   524	    msCellObservable OA OB (msConstraintVars i 0) *
   525	        msCellObservable OA OB (msConstraintVars i 1) *
   526	    msCellObservable OA OB (msConstraintVars i 2) =
   527	      if i = 5 then -1 else 1 := by
   528	  have hAB := anti_mul_sq OA OB hOA hOB hac
   529	  have hZX := anti_mul_sq qubitZ qubitX qubitZ_sq qubitX_sq (by
   530	    rw [qubitX_mul_qubitZ]
   531	    simp)
   532	  fin_cases i <;>
   533	    simp [msConstraintVars, msCellObservable, heteroKron_mul, hOA, hOB,
   534	      qubitX_sq, qubitZ_sq, qubitX_mul_qubitZ, hAB, hZX,
   535	      heteroKron_neg_left, heteroKron_neg_right,
   536	      heteroKron_one_one]
   537	
   538	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for
   539	`exists_ms_perfect_strategy_of_anticommuting` (`thm:ms-from-ac`, blueprint
   540	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:257-267`): the two effects of a binary projective
   541	measurement are orthogonal idempotents: their product is the common effect when
   542	the outcomes agree and `0` otherwise. -/
   543	theorem binary_effect_mul
   544	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
   545	    (M : Measurement (ZMod 2) V)
   546	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M)
   547	    (a b : ZMod 2) :
   548	    M.effect a * M.effect b = if a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
   549	  rcases binary_effects_orthogonal M hM with ⟨h01, h10⟩
   550	  rcases zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one a with rfl | rfl <;>
   551	    rcases zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one b with rfl | rfl <;>
   552	      simp [(hM _).isIdempotentElem.eq, h01, h10]
   553	
   554	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for
   555	`exists_ms_perfect_strategy_of_anticommuting` (`thm:ms-from-ac`, blueprint
   556	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:257-267`): the reflection effects of two commuting Hermitian
   557	involutions commute. -/
   558	theorem reflectionEffect_commute
   559	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
   560	    {O P : Op V} (hOP : Commute O P) (a b : ZMod 2) :
   561	    Commute (reflectionEffect O a) (reflectionEffect P b) := by
   562	  rw [commute_iff_eq]
   563	  rcases zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one a with rfl | rfl <;>
   564	    rcases zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one b with rfl | rfl <;>
   565	      simp only [reflectionEffect, if_pos, if_neg one_ne_zero]
   566	  all_goals rw [smul_mul_smul, smul_mul_smul]
   567	  all_goals congr 1
   568	  all_goals noncomm_ring [hOP.eq]
   569	
   570	private theorem reflectionEffect_commute_obs
   571	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
   572	    {O P : Op V} (hOP : Commute O P) (a : ZMod 2) :
   573	    Commute (reflectionEffect O a) P := by
   574	  rw [commute_iff_eq]
   575	  rcases zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one a with rfl | rfl <;>
   576	    simp only [reflectionEffect, if_pos, if_neg one_ne_zero]
   577	  all_goals rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm]
   578	  all_goals congr 1
   579	  all_goals noncomm_ring [hOP.eq]

   581	private theorem reflectionEffect_mul_obs_zero
   582	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
   583	    (O : Op V) (hO : O * O = 1) :
   584	    reflectionEffect O 0 * O = reflectionEffect O 0 := by
   585	  simp only [reflectionEffect, if_pos]
   586	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, add_mul, one_mul, hO]
   587	  module
   588	
   589	private theorem reflectionEffect_mul_obs_one
   590	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
   591	    (O : Op V) (hO : O * O = 1) :
   592	    reflectionEffect O 1 * O = -reflectionEffect O 1 := by
   593	  simp only [reflectionEffect, if_neg one_ne_zero]
   594	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, sub_mul, one_mul, hO]
   595	  module
   596	
   597	private theorem mul_reflectionEffect_zero_of_eigen_pos
   598	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
   599	    (E O : Op V) (hEO : E * O = E) :
   600	    E * reflectionEffect O 0 = E := by
   601	  simp only [reflectionEffect, if_pos]
   602	  rw [mul_smul_comm, mul_add, mul_one, hEO]
   603	  module
   604	
   605	private theorem mul_reflectionEffect_one_of_eigen_neg
   606	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
   607	    (E O : Op V) (hEO : E * O = -E) :
   608	    E * reflectionEffect O 1 = E := by
   609	  simp only [reflectionEffect, if_neg one_ne_zero]
   610	  rw [mul_smul_comm, mul_sub, mul_one, hEO]
   611	  module
   612	
   613	private theorem reflection_pair_mul_observables
   614	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
   615	    (P0 P1 O0 O1 : Op V) (s0 s1 : ℂ)
   616	    (h10 : Commute P1 O0)
   617	    (h0 : P0 * O0 = s0 • P0) (h1 : P1 * O1 = s1 • P1) :
   618	    (P0 * P1) * (O0 * O1) = (s0 * s1) • (P0 * P1) := by
   619	  calc
   620	    (P0 * P1) * (O0 * O1) = P0 * (P1 * O0) * O1 := by noncomm_ring
   621	    _ = P0 * (O0 * P1) * O1 := by rw [h10.eq]
   622	    _ = (P0 * O0) * (P1 * O1) := by noncomm_ring
   623	    _ = (s0 • P0) * (s1 • P1) := by rw [h0, h1]
   624	    _ = (s0 * s1) • (P0 * P1) := by rw [smul_mul_smul]
   625	
   626	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for
   627	`exists_ms_perfect_strategy_of_anticommuting` (`thm:ms-from-ac`, blueprint
   628	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:257-267`): if `O0` and `O1` are commuting involutions and
   629	the product `O0 * O1 * O2` equals `(-1) ^ p`, then the third reflection effect
   630	taken at the outcome `p - b0 - b1` forced by the parity acts as the identity on
   631	the product of the first two reflection effects. -/
   632	theorem reflection_pair_absorbs_parity_effect
   633	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
   634	    (O0 O1 O2 : Op V)
   635	    (hO0 : O0 * O0 = 1) (hO1 : O1 * O1 = 1)
   636	    (h01 : Commute O0 O1)
   637	    (p b0 b1 : ZMod 2)
   638	    (hp : (p = 0 ∧ O0 * O1 * O2 = 1) ∨
   639	      (p = 1 ∧ O0 * O1 * O2 = -1)) :
   640	    (reflectionEffect O0 b0 * reflectionEffect O1 b1) *
   641	        reflectionEffect O2 (p - b0 - b1) =
   642	      reflectionEffect O0 b0 * reflectionEffect O1 b1 := by
   643	  rcases hp with ⟨rfl, hprod⟩ | ⟨rfl, hprod⟩
   644	  · have hO2eq : O2 = O0 * O1 := by
   645	      calc
   646	        O2 = (O0 * O0) * (O1 * O1) * O2 := by rw [hO0, hO1]; simp
   647	        _ = O0 * (O0 * O1) * O1 * O2 := by noncomm_ring
   648	        _ = O0 * (O1 * O0) * O1 * O2 := by rw [h01.eq]
   649	        _ = O0 * O1 * (O0 * O1 * O2) := by noncomm_ring
   650	        _ = O0 * O1 := by rw [hprod]; simp
   651	    rcases zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one b0 with rfl | rfl <;>
   652	      rcases zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one b1 with rfl | rfl
   653	    · apply mul_reflectionEffect_zero_of_eigen_pos
   654	      rw [hO2eq]
   655	      simpa using reflection_pair_mul_observables
   656	        (reflectionEffect O0 0) (reflectionEffect O1 0) O0 O1 1 1
   657	        (reflectionEffect_commute_obs h01.symm 0)
   658	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_zero O0 hO0)
   659	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_zero O1 hO1)
   660	    · apply mul_reflectionEffect_one_of_eigen_neg
   661	      rw [hO2eq]
   662	      simpa using reflection_pair_mul_observables
   663	        (reflectionEffect O0 0) (reflectionEffect O1 1) O0 O1 1 (-1)
   664	        (reflectionEffect_commute_obs h01.symm 1)
   665	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_zero O0 hO0)
   666	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_one O1 hO1)
   667	    · apply mul_reflectionEffect_one_of_eigen_neg
   668	      rw [hO2eq]
   669	      simpa using reflection_pair_mul_observables
   670	        (reflectionEffect O0 1) (reflectionEffect O1 0) O0 O1 (-1) 1
   671	        (reflectionEffect_commute_obs h01.symm 0)
   672	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_one O0 hO0)
   673	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_zero O1 hO1)
   674	    · apply mul_reflectionEffect_zero_of_eigen_pos
   675	      rw [hO2eq]
   676	      simpa using reflection_pair_mul_observables
   677	        (reflectionEffect O0 1) (reflectionEffect O1 1) O0 O1 (-1) (-1)
   678	        (reflectionEffect_commute_obs h01.symm 1)
   679	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_one O0 hO0)
   680	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_one O1 hO1)
   681	  · have hO2eq : O2 = -(O0 * O1) := by
   682	      calc
   683	        O2 = (O0 * O0) * (O1 * O1) * O2 := by rw [hO0, hO1]; simp
   684	        _ = O0 * (O0 * O1) * O1 * O2 := by noncomm_ring
   685	        _ = O0 * (O1 * O0) * O1 * O2 := by rw [h01.eq]
   686	        _ = O0 * O1 * (O0 * O1 * O2) := by noncomm_ring
   687	        _ = -(O0 * O1) := by rw [hprod]; simp
   688	    rcases zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one b0 with rfl | rfl <;>
   689	      rcases zmod_two_eq_zero_or_one b1 with rfl | rfl
   690	    · apply mul_reflectionEffect_one_of_eigen_neg
   691	      rw [hO2eq, mul_neg]
   692	      have hpair := reflection_pair_mul_observables
   693	        (reflectionEffect O0 0) (reflectionEffect O1 0) O0 O1 1 1
   694	        (reflectionEffect_commute_obs h01.symm 0)
   695	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_zero O0 hO0)
   696	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_zero O1 hO1)
   697	      rw [hpair]
   698	      simp
   699	    · apply mul_reflectionEffect_zero_of_eigen_pos
   700	      rw [hO2eq, mul_neg]
   701	      have hpair := reflection_pair_mul_observables
   702	        (reflectionEffect O0 0) (reflectionEffect O1 1) O0 O1 1 (-1)
   703	        (reflectionEffect_commute_obs h01.symm 1)
   704	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_zero O0 hO0)
   705	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_one O1 hO1)
   706	      rw [hpair]
   707	      simp
   708	    · apply mul_reflectionEffect_zero_of_eigen_pos
   709	      rw [hO2eq, mul_neg]
   710	      have hpair := reflection_pair_mul_observables
   711	        (reflectionEffect O0 1) (reflectionEffect O1 0) O0 O1 (-1) 1
   712	        (reflectionEffect_commute_obs h01.symm 0)
   713	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_one O0 hO0)
   714	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_zero O1 hO1)
   715	      rw [hpair]
   716	      simp
   717	    · apply mul_reflectionEffect_one_of_eigen_neg
   718	      rw [hO2eq, mul_neg]
   719	      have hpair := reflection_pair_mul_observables
   720	        (reflectionEffect O0 1) (reflectionEffect O1 1) O0 O1 (-1) (-1)
   721	        (reflectionEffect_commute_obs h01.symm 1)
   722	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_one O0 hO0)
   723	        (by simpa using reflectionEffect_mul_obs_one O1 hO1)
   724	      rw [hpair]
   725	      simp
   726	
   727	end

     3	/-!
     4	# Perfect strategies for the Magic Square game
     5	
     6	This file completes the construction of `thm:ms-from-ac`.  It identifies the
     7	question pairs in the support of the Magic Square distribution, shows that the
     8	measurement family commutes there and annihilates rejected answer pairs on the
     9	EPR state, evaluates the Born weights of the accepted answers, and assembles a
    10	symmetric SPCC strategy of value one from an anticommuting consistent pair of
    11	binary measurements.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	The source statement is `thm:ms-from-ac` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:257-267`, from
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:654-722`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum

    28	private theorem msConstraintVars_injective (i : Fin 6) :
    29	    Function.Injective (msConstraintVars i) := by
    30	  intro k l h
    31	  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases k <;> fin_cases l <;>
    32	    simp [msConstraintVars] at h ⊢
    33	
    34	private theorem msConstraintVars_exists_iff
    35	    (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2) (b : ZMod 2) :
    36	    (∃ l : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i l = msConstraintVars i k ∧ β l = b) ↔
    37	      β k = b := by
    38	  constructor
    39	  · rintro ⟨l, hl, hlb⟩
    40	    rwa [msConstraintVars_injective i hl] at hlb
    41	  · intro h
    42	    exact ⟨k, rfl, h⟩

    44	private theorem msStrategyMeasurement_incident_commute
    45	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    46	    (P : Fin 9 → Measurement (ZMod 2) V)
    47	    (hP : ∀ j, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (P j))
    48	    (hcomm : ∀ i k l a b,
    49	      Commute ((P (msConstraintVars i k)).effect a)
    50	        ((P (msConstraintVars i l)).effect b))
    51	    (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) (a b : MsAnswer) :
    52	    Commute ((msStrategyMeasurement P hP hcomm (.constraint i)).effect a)
    53	      ((msStrategyMeasurement P hP hcomm
    54	        (.var (msConstraintVars i k))).effect b) := by
    55	  by_cases ha : a ∈ Set.range (fun ab => MsAnswer.triple (parityTriple i ab))
    56	  · rcases ha with ⟨ab, rfl⟩
    57	    rw [msStrategyMeasurement_constraint_triple]
    58	    by_cases hb : b ∈ Set.range (MsAnswer.bit : ZMod 2 → MsAnswer)
    59	    · rcases hb with ⟨c, rfl⟩
    60	      rw [msStrategyMeasurement_var_bit]
    61	      change Commute
    62	        ((P (msConstraintVars i 0)).effect ab.1 *
    63	          (P (msConstraintVars i 1)).effect ab.2)
    64	        ((P (msConstraintVars i k)).effect c)
    65	      exact (hcomm i 0 k ab.1 c).mul_left (hcomm i 1 k ab.2 c)
    66	    · rw [msStrategyMeasurement_var_zero _ _ _ _ hb]
    67	      exact Commute.zero_right _
    68	  · rw [msStrategyMeasurement_constraint_zero _ _ _ _ ha]
    69	    exact Commute.zero_left _

    71	private theorem msStrategyMeasurement_rejected_mul
    72	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    73	    (P : Fin 9 → Measurement (ZMod 2) V)
    74	    (hP : ∀ j, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (P j))
    75	    (hcomm : ∀ i k l a b,
    76	      Commute ((P (msConstraintVars i k)).effect a)
    77	        ((P (msConstraintVars i l)).effect b))
    78	    (hmul : ∀ i k ab b,
    79	      (msConstraintJoint P hP hcomm i).effect ab *
    80	          (P (msConstraintVars i k)).effect b =
    81	        if parityTriple i ab k = b then
    82	          (msConstraintJoint P hP hcomm i).effect ab else 0)
    83	    (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) (a b : MsAnswer)
    84	    (hrej : msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) a b = false) :
    85	    ((msStrategyMeasurement P hP hcomm (.constraint i)).effect a) *
    86	      ((msStrategyMeasurement P hP hcomm
    87	        (.var (msConstraintVars i k))).effect b) = 0 := by
    88	  by_cases ha : a ∈ Set.range (fun ab => MsAnswer.triple (parityTriple i ab))
    89	  · rcases ha with ⟨ab, rfl⟩
    90	    rw [msStrategyMeasurement_constraint_triple]
    91	    by_cases hb : b ∈ Set.range (MsAnswer.bit : ZMod 2 → MsAnswer)
    92	    · rcases hb with ⟨c, rfl⟩
    93	      rw [msStrategyMeasurement_var_bit]
    94	      have hne : parityTriple i ab k ≠ c := by
    95	        simpa [msWinPredicate, parityTriple_sum,
    96	          msConstraintVars_exists_iff] using hrej
    97	      rw [hmul i k ab c]
    98	      simp [hne]
    99	    · rw [msStrategyMeasurement_var_zero _ _ _ _ hb]
   100	      simp
   101	  · rw [msStrategyMeasurement_constraint_zero _ _ _ _ ha]
   102	    simp

   104	private theorem msStrategyMeasurement_rejected_mul_reverse
   105	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
   106	    (P : Fin 9 → Measurement (ZMod 2) V)
   107	    (hP : ∀ j, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (P j))
   108	    (hcomm : ∀ i k l a b,
   109	      Commute ((P (msConstraintVars i k)).effect a)
   110	        ((P (msConstraintVars i l)).effect b))
   111	    (hmul : ∀ i k ab b,
   112	      (msConstraintJoint P hP hcomm i).effect ab *
   113	          (P (msConstraintVars i k)).effect b =
   114	        if parityTriple i ab k = b then
   115	          (msConstraintJoint P hP hcomm i).effect ab else 0)
   116	    (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) (a b : MsAnswer)
   117	    (hrej : msWinPredicate (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) (.constraint i) a b = false) :
   118	    ((msStrategyMeasurement P hP hcomm

   125	private theorem msGame_support_incidence (x y : MsType)
   126	    (hxy : (x, y) ∈ msGameSymm.μ.support) :
   127	    (∃ i : Fin 6, ∃ k : Fin 3,
   128	      x = .constraint i ∧ y = .var (msConstraintVars i k)) ∨
   129	      ∃ i : Fin 6, ∃ k : Fin 3,
   130	        x = .var (msConstraintVars i k) ∧ y = .constraint i := by
   131	  change (x, y) ∈
   132	    Finset.univ.filter (fun ab : MsType × MsType =>
   133	      Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges) at hxy
   134	  have hedge : Sym2.mk x y ∈ msEdges := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hxy).2
   135	  rw [msEdges] at hedge
   136	  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hedge with ⟨⟨i, k⟩, _, hik⟩
   137	  rcases Sym2.eq_iff.mp hik with hik | hik
   138	  · left
   139	    exact ⟨i, k, hik.1.symm, hik.2.symm⟩
   140	  · right
   141	    exact ⟨i, k, hik.2.symm, hik.1.symm⟩

   143	private theorem msGame_positive_incidence (x y : MsType)
   144	    (hxy : 0 < msGameSymm.μ.weight (x, y)) :
   145	    (∃ i : Fin 6, ∃ k : Fin 3,
   146	      x = .constraint i ∧ y = .var (msConstraintVars i k)) ∨
   147	      ∃ i : Fin 6, ∃ k : Fin 3,
   148	        x = .var (msConstraintVars i k) ∧ y = .constraint i := by
   149	  apply msGame_support_incidence x y
   150	  by_contra hnot
   151	  rw [msGameSymm.μ.outsideSupport (x, y) hnot] at hxy
   152	  exact (lt_irrefl 0 hxy)

   154	private theorem msStrategyMeasurement_commuting
   155	    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
   156	    (P : Fin 9 → Measurement (ZMod 2) V)
   157	    (hP : ∀ j, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (P j))
   158	    (hcomm : ∀ i k l a b,
   159	      Commute ((P (msConstraintVars i k)).effect a)
   160	        ((P (msConstraintVars i l)).effect b)) :
   161	    IsCommutingOn msGameSymm.μ
   162	      (msStrategyMeasurement P hP hcomm)
   163	      (msStrategyMeasurement P hP hcomm) := by
   164	  intro x y hxy a b
   165	  rcases msGame_positive_incidence x y hxy with hxy | hxy
   166	  · rcases hxy with ⟨i, k, rfl, rfl⟩
   167	    exact msStrategyMeasurement_incident_commute P hP hcomm i k a b
   168	  · rcases hxy with ⟨i, k, rfl, rfl⟩
   169	    exact (msStrategyMeasurement_incident_commute P hP hcomm i k b a).symm

## 5. Review Checklist

Every PR touching Lean code should be reviewed against these criteria:

1. **Proof correctness** -- No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.
   Run `rg -n "sorry|axiom" <file>` to verify.

2. **Mathlib style** -- Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and
   `MATHLIB_doc` references. See the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review`
   reference for the full Mathlib review guide.

3. **Paper terminology** -- Public Lean names, module docstrings, declaration
   docstrings, and documentation-visible comments should use terminology from
   the paper and blueprint, not implementation history. See
   [mathematical_language.md](mathematical_language.md) for the project-local
   language rule for Lean documentation and public names. Reviewers should flag
   names that encode historical formalization status rather than mathematical
   content. When an old public identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR,
   record the required migration in the issue, PR description, or an audit file
   under [audits/](../audits/).
   New and substantively updated audit files should follow the term norm and
   format in
   [audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md](../audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md).
   Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   public name.
   Review-fix PRs must read the relevant audit files under [audits/](../audits/)
   before changing names or prose. If an audit marks a naming migration or
   historical-formalization term as in scope for the fix, addressing it or
   explicitly updating the audit trail is a merge blocker.

4. **Linter hygiene** -- Linter-warning cleanup must fix warnings, not mask
   them with broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks. See
   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md#linter-warnings) for the project rule and the narrow
   exception policy.

5. **Type safety** -- No universe mismatches, coercion problems, or unresolved
   metavariables.

6. **Performance** -- Avoid expensive tactics on large types (e.g., `decide` on
   `Fin 1000`). Watch for timeout-prone proof terms.

7. **Modularity** -- Are new lemmas general enough to be reused? Could any be
   upstreamed to Mathlib?

8. **Documentation** -- Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.
   Module files should have a header comment with `## References` citing the
   relevant arXiv paper(s).

9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** -- If the PR formalizes a statement
   boundedness/normalization, completeness where applicable) encoded directly
   in the structure or constructor, rather than deferred to downstream lemmas?
4. **Stress-test check** -- Is at least one nontrivial theorem in scope of the
   PR provable/stated against the scaffold without adding ad hoc assumptions?

If any answer is "no", treat the scaffold as unsafe and request a follow-up
before broad theorem layering continues.

## 6. Lean Code Style

This project follows Mathlib conventions with project-specific additions.

### Reference guides

Shared references (the `lean-conventions` skill of
texra-ai/texra-lean-skills, auto-installed via `.claude/settings.json`):

- **Documentation style**: the `MATHLIB_doc` reference -- module headers,
  docstrings, LaTeX in comments, sectioning comments.
- **Naming conventions**: the `MATHLIB_naming` reference -- capitalization
  rules, symbol-to-name dictionary, variable conventions.
- **Review guide**: the `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference -- detailed examples of
  style, documentation, location, and improvement considerations.

MIPStarRE-local references:

- **Mathematical language**: [mathematical_language.md](mathematical_language.md)
  -- project-local terminology rules for Lean names and documentation.
- **Proof integrity**: the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference plus
  the addenda in [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md) -- blocker
  and warning patterns for proof correctness.
- **Blueprint style**: [blueprint_style_guide.md](blueprint_style_guide.md) --
  notation and section conventions for the active blueprint.

### Project-specific conventions

**Module header**: Every `.lean` file should start with a module docstring that
includes:

```lean
/-!
# Title

Summary of what this file contains.

## Main definitions / statements

- `FooBar` : description
- `fooBar_baz` : description

## References

- [arXiv:XXXX.XXXXX](https://arxiv.org/abs/XXXX.XXXXX) -- Author, *Title*
-/
```

**Docstrings**: Required on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant
`theorem`. Encouraged on supporting lemmas. Use Markdown; refer to Lean
identifiers in backticks.

**Sectioning comments**: Use `/-! ### Section Title -/` to organize long files
into logical sections.

**Variable naming**: Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` reference. For
this project specifically:
- `q` for alphabet size / finite field order
- `n`, `m` for dimension parameters
- `σ` for strategies
- `P` for projective measurements
- `G` for graphs (hypercube expansion)

## 7. CI & Automation

The following workflows run automatically:

| Workflow | Trigger | What it does |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| **Lean CI** (`pr-ci.yml` (`build` job)) | Push to `main`, PRs touching `.lean`/`lakefile.toml`/`lean-toolchain` | Runs `lake build` with Mathlib cache |
| **PR Review** (`pr-review.yml`, `code-review` jobs) | After a successful PR CI run | Automated review for proof integrity, Mathlib style, type safety, performance, modularity, mathematical exposition, and documentation |
| **Issue Automation** (`issue-automation.yml`) | Issue opened/labeled/closed/reopened; PR opened/merged | Classifies new issues, posts Mathlib scouting reports, keeps tracking issues current via a deterministic script (progress comments, sub-issue counts, and a ready-to-close notice when every sub-issue is resolved), and scans merged PRs for genuine deferred mathematical obligations, filing `follow-up` issues |
| **Blueprint Lint** (`pr-ci.yml` (`blueprint-render` job)) | PRs touching blueprint files | Builds `leanblueprint pdf` / `web` to catch broken labels, undefined macros, and plasTeX errors, then runs the blueprint ↔ Lean sync checks. The LaTeX convention scan and the `scripts/tests` helper unit tests both run locally in the pre-commit hook. |
| **Blueprint Sync & Prose Review** (`pr-review.yml`, `prose-review` job) | After a successful PR CI run | Reviews blueprint synchronization, source-faithfulness, and mathematical prose for formalization changes. |
| **README Freshness Audit** (`housekeeping.yml`, `readme-freshness` job) | Weekly + manual dispatch | Report-only audit for README local paths, LDT submodule count, and hard-coded Lean/Mathlib versions |
| **PR Mathematical Description** (`pr-cleanup.yml`) | PR opened from `claude/*` or `codex/*` branches | Normalizes title to `type(scope): desc`, rewrites the PR body as a self-contained mathematical note, preserves source citations from the linked issue, copies labels, adds `Addresses #N`, and comments on the issue |
| **Mathlib Scout** (`issue-automation.yml`, `scout` job) | Formalization issue opened/labeled | Scouts Mathlib for relevant lemmas and posts a scouting report |

### What CI checks before merge

- `lake build MIPStarRE` must succeed (no type errors, no broken imports).
- No new `sorry` without explicit justification.
- Blueprint labels must resolve (no broken `\ref` or `\label`).
- Claude Code Review should not flag critical issues (proof correctness,
  type safety).
